items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: Walter O’Keefe to me was like a Fred Allen or a Jack Benny. Very funny.

ctx.x: Put his name down. He was one of the greats. Walter O’Keefe to me was like a Fred Allen or a Jack Benny. Very funny. In the show a guy comes up to Walter O’Keefe, he says, “I haven’t seen you in years.” And Walter O’Keefe would say, “it’s been longer than that, it’s been months.” No that sounds funny in the show. And then he says to Walter O’Keefe in the show, he says, “you know, if I woulda hung out with you, if I woulda been with you we woulda made millions.” And Walter O’Keefe says, “more than that, we would…

But why the show never came to New York I’ll never know. And Vernon Duke wrote the music. He wrote a song where we used the song — oh thank you sir. You see I understand Indian language. You’re terrific, Tim, I like you. He wrote a song that you woulda loved, Monk, called “Low and Lazy” which she sang with her negligee, Dolores Gray. She came out on the corner of the stage with a pin spotlight, is that what you call it?
